title: Honor D-Bus idle inhibits on the paths Chromium actually calls
head: 606bd454f093
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Settings package omits the unit's vendor path required by its packaging fixture
leads.consequence: The installed omarchy package installs the new daemon and probe from its bin glob, while the current omarchy-settings PKGBUILD omits an explicit /usr/lib/systemd/user install for the unit. Its separate `cp -a default/.` does ship a fallback copy under /usr/share/omarchy/default, so first-run usually links and enables that fallback if both packages are built from the same commit. Nevertheless config-test's package-default coverage fails at this head; every user gets a persistent user-path linked unit instead of the advertised vendor unit. If the source really is unavailable or enable fails, `|| true` lets first-run complete without retrying later. Coordinate omarchy-pkgs#210 and test the actual installed-source and failure cases.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus (c2); published as still present

leads.summary: Checkout fallback can overwrite a user's unit and permanently shadow the packaged one
leads.consequence: When the vendor unit is absent but the checkout has it, ln -sfn replaces a preexisting regular user service file at the same name without asking. It then installs a user-level symlink pointing to the current absolute $OMARCHY_PATH, higher priority than /usr/lib/systemd/user. After a later package starts installing the vendor unit, the user link is not removed or repointed. A stable packaged source at /usr/share/omarchy/default updates with the settings package, but dev unlink or checkout move/removal can leave a dangling or stale higher-priority user link instead of switching to the vendor copy. Preserve an existing user unit; when upgrading, remove only a symlink proven to be Omarchy's checkout fallback.
leads.triage: dropped: improbable pre-existing unit of new name; dev-link case unverified hypothesis (also Opus H2)

leads.summary: A recycled unrelated PID authenticates a stale inhibitor state
leads.consequence: After daemon death leaves a state file with count > 0, kill -0 accepts an unrelated process that later gets that PID. On the next probe (e.g. shell start), stale JSON is returned and the shell disables idle/screensaver/lock even with no ScreenSaver owner. The new test exercises only a definitely dead PID. Compare PID creation time and ownership of the D-Bus name (or give state a session/token) before trusting it.
leads.triage: dropped: pre-existing, needs daemon crash without clean publish plus pid reuse inside a tmpfs runtime dir; low value

leads.summary: Changed crash test never kills a live client
leads.consequence: crash.py makes an Inhibit request and returns immediately; the scenario waits 0.8 seconds before kill -9 of its PID. The test therefore checks cleanup on an ordinary D-Bus disconnect rather than the promised forced termination; a regression specific to killed clients would pass. Keep the client alive after publishing its cookie, confirm it is still live, then signal and assert disconnect cleanup.
leads.triage: verified factually (no sleep in crash.py) but dropped: exit and kill both disconnect; test intent still exercised

leads.summary: A state change during an already running probe can be dropped until another write
leads.consequence: If the probe has already read the previous state, a directory event restarts the 50 ms debounce, but its callback fires while Process.running is true, refreshInhibitorState returns without queueing. onExited calls FileView.reload, which reattaches the watcher but does not request a second probe. With no further directory write, the shell keeps the old count, potentially delaying the screensaver/lock after an inhibitor arrives or suppressing them after release. Queue one pending refresh when an update arrives during a running probe, then run it on exit.
leads.triage: sent to Opus (followup-1.md): mechanism real, loses updates only when a probe run exceeds the 50 ms debounce; 0/795 at realistic timing; not published

leads.summary: Open Firefox idle PR and alternate D-Bus PR need explicit reconciliation
leads.consequence: Open #8955 also changes idleEnabled, adds MPRIS gating and tests requiring IdleModel.idleEnabledAfter, whereas #13359 requires dbusInhibitorCount === 0. A PR-specific-base git merge-file produces conflict markers in Service.qml, IdleModel.js and idle-test.sh; selecting either side's predicate drops the other feature or fails its text fixture. Open #6572 separately introduces another implementation with the same daemon binary and unit names: choose one approach, not two daemons competing for the same ScreenSaver name. Preserve both independent inhibitor predicates and both sets of tests if #8955 merges.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus (d4); #8955 published as still present; #6572 not published

leads.summary: Open first-run unit PR rejects this PR's retained batch enable
leads.consequence: Open #10582 makes every first-run unit an individual enable with warning handling and its new test explicitly fails if a multi-name `enable --now \` batch remains. #13359 retains the batch and adds only the inhibitor unit separately; a git merge-file using #10582's merge base produces conflicting hunks. Resolve the batch to the per-unit loop and update #13359's awk/grep fixture to assert the actual setup semantics, otherwise #10582's test fails or its missing-unit fix disappears.
leads.triage: verified factually (gh: open, rewrites same batch); published as optional note with Opus self-check correction (conflict claim removed)

leads.summary: A failed state write still returns a successful Inhibit cookie
leads.consequence: If runtime state cannot be written (full filesystem, inaccessible state directory or file), after_change logs OSError but handle_inhibit returns a cookie anyway. The app believes video is inhibited although the shell still reads zero or stale state, so the screensaver/lock may interrupt playback. UnInhibit can also leave stale count after write failure. Return a D-Bus error and roll back newly added cookie when publishing the state fails, and handle clear failures so they cannot silently pin idle.
leads.triage: dropped: pre-existing, unchanged since earlier review, rare runtime-dir write failure

leads.summary: First-run unit inventory in file-layout docs omits the new service
leads.consequence: The documentation explicitly lists the units enabled by first-run but does not include omarchy-idle-inhibit.service. Someone debugging a fresh install is not told to check this mandatory session service, particularly important while the package vendor path is missing. Add omarchy-idle-inhibit.service to the first-run list near omarchy-crash-watch.service, and mention the fallback/packaging dependency until #210 ships.
leads.triage: verified (list also omits owed already); not published, low value

leads.summary: User idle manual does not describe the newly automatic D-Bus inhibitor
leads.consequence: The manual lists idle timing and Stay Awake as the controls but does not say when apps can stop both screensaver and lock via D-Bus, how to see current holders, or that PowerManagement-only audio requests do not inhibit the screen. Users troubleshooting a long-running blank screen after video playback have no pointer to omarchy debug idle or the new daemon. Add a concise explanation and diagnostics command under Idle.

limits: No Quickshell window/session or browsers were allocated; H5 is a source-derived conditional sequence, not a measured QML reproducer. Firefox's packaged-version D-Bus path and version-specific VLC source were not established, and no issue rests on either claim. Other topic-search PRs outside the four overlapping PRs were not exhaustively diff-read; do not treat this hunt as a comprehensive all-open-PR merge simulation.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** At `606bd454` new first-run code breaks `owe-integration-test.sh` without `OMARCHY_PATH`. [Earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13359#issuecomment-5852245186) status:

- **Resolved:** PowerManagement count, missing-dir watcher, first-run batch, dead-pid test.
- **Still present:** `config-test.sh` fails until omarchy-pkgs#210 (or equivalent) lands; stale-holder and #8955 notes unchanged.

### `owe-integration-test.sh` now needs `OMARCHY_PATH`

`enable-user-units.sh` runs under `set -u` and now reads `$OMARCHY_PATH`; the test sets only `HOME` and `PATH`. Without `OMARCHY_PATH` exported (e.g. a clean sandbox) it fails with `unbound variable`; it passed at `45cadff4`. With it set, the fallback link can land in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, outside the test home.

**Suggested change:** pass `XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$work/home/.config" OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT"` at `owe-integration-test.sh:56`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 606bd454)</summary>

`test/shell.d/owe-integration-test.sh` runs `install/user/first-run/enable-user-units.sh` with only `HOME` and `PATH` overridden. The script runs under `set -u`, and 606bd454 adds a reference to `$OMARCHY_PATH` (line 29), so the test now depends on the caller's environment.

Run from a checkout of the PR head (606bd454), with `OMARCHY_PATH` not set:

```console
$ cd /tmp/omarchy && env -u OMARCHY_PATH -u XDG_CONFIG_HOME bash test/shell.d/owe-integration-test.sh | tail -2
/tmp/omarchy/install/user/first-run/enable-user-units.sh: line 29: OMARCHY_PATH: unbound variable
Enable OWE desktop video backgrounds and lock feed
ok - a failed live service start fails the migration
[exit status: 1]
```

The same command at the previously reviewed head (45cadff4):

```console
$ cd /tmp/omarchy && env -u OMARCHY_PATH -u XDG_CONFIG_HOME bash test/shell.d/owe-integration-test.sh | tail -2
ok - lock posters are cached, refreshed after source changes, and old frames are evicted
ok - failed poster generation never publishes a partial image
[exit status: 0]
```

With `OMARCHY_PATH` set and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` pointing outside the test's temporary `HOME`, the test passes but the first-run fallback writes its unit symlink into that directory (no packaged `/usr/lib/systemd/user/omarchy-idle-inhibit.service` on the machine):

```console
$ cd /tmp/omarchy && OMARCHY_PATH=/tmp/omarchy XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/xdg-demo bash test/shell.d/owe-integration-test.sh | tail -1; find /tmp/xdg-demo -type l -printf '%p -> %l\n'
ok - failed poster generation never publishes a partial image
/tmp/xdg-demo/systemd/user/omarchy-idle-inhibit.service -> /tmp/omarchy/default/systemd/user/omarchy-idle-inhibit.service
[exit status: 0]
```

Suggested test change (following docs/testing.md, "Fake `$HOME`, real `$OMARCHY_PATH`"):

```diff
 : >"$TEST_CALLS"
-HOME="$work/home" PATH="$work/bin:$PATH" bash "$ROOT/install/user/first-run/enable-user-units.sh"
+HOME="$work/home" XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$work/home/.config" OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" PATH="$work/bin:$PATH" bash "$ROOT/install/user/first-run/enable-user-units.sh"
 grep -E '^systemctl --user enable --now .*owed.service' "$TEST_CALLS" >/dev/null
```

With that change, at 606bd454:

```console
$ cd /tmp/omarchy && env -u OMARCHY_PATH -u XDG_CONFIG_HOME bash test/shell.d/owe-integration-test.sh | tail -1
ok - failed poster generation never publishes a partial image
[exit status: 0]

$ cd /tmp/omarchy && XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/xdg-demo bash test/shell.d/owe-integration-test.sh | tail -1; find /tmp/xdg-demo -type l | wc -l
ok - failed poster generation never publishes a partial image
0
[exit status: 0]
```

(`[exit status: N]` is the exit status of the whole pipeline, run with `pipefail`.)
</details>

<details><summary>Earlier findings in detail</summary>

- **PowerManagement counted toward idle: resolved.** Only `org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver` is owned now. In Chromium 152 `power_save_blocker_linux.cc`, an unowned PowerManagement name is skipped with no fallback to ScreenSaver, and video wake locks still go to ScreenSaver. On a private bus, a PowerManagement `Inhibit` gets `ServiceUnknown` and a ScreenSaver `Inhibit` returns a cookie. The new test fails when the name is owned again.
- **Watcher armed on a missing directory: resolved.** Quickshell v0.3.1 `reload()` re-creates the watch on the path and its parent, and `fileChanged` comes only from watcher events, so the reload in `onExited` cannot loop. In a syscall-level replica of the FileView and Qt watch setup (not Quickshell itself), the "shell first" order sees the held inhibit at `606bd454` and missed it at `45cadff4`.
- **Unit in the first-run batch: resolved.** With a stubbed `systemctl`, the batch no longer names the unit, and the unit is enabled separately (linked first when the packaged unit is missing). On packaged installs the link target is omarchy-settings' copy under `/usr/share/omarchy/default/`.
- **Packaging line: still present.** `config-test.sh` fails against omarchy-pkgs `master` with `PKGBUILD does not explicitly install default/systemd/user/omarchy-idle-inhibit.service`, and passes with the #210 hunk applied. GitHub reports #210 as not mergeable, and the code comment in its PKGBUILD hunk still says the unit owns PowerManagement.
- **Dead-pid test: resolved.** A probe without the `kill -0` check now fails the test.
- **PowerManagement owned elsewhere: resolved.** The daemon no longer requests that name.
- **Stale holders after the daemon dies and stays down: unchanged.** The probe script and `omarchy-debug-idle` still behave as before.
- **Open #8955: still present.** It rewrites the same `idleEnabled` line and pins that text in its test.
</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer: packaging line (fails at 606bd454)</summary>

### Reproducer: `config-test.sh` still fails against current omarchy-pkgs

`test/shell.d/config-test.sh` requires the omarchy-settings PKGBUILD to install `default/systemd/user/omarchy-idle-inhibit.service` to `/usr/lib/systemd/user/`. Run at the PR head (606bd454) with `OMARCHY_PKGS_PATH` pointing at an omarchy-pkgs checkout of `master` (660cbe39):

```console
$ cd /tmp/omarchy && PATH=/tmp/omarchy/bin:$PATH OMARCHY_PKGS_PATH=/tmp/omarchy-pkgs bash test/shell.d/config-test.sh 2>&1 | tail -3
ok - default right layout keeps agents next to the tray
ok - default bar widget ids resolve to manifests and entry points
PKGBUILD does not explicitly install default/systemd/user/omarchy-idle-inhibit.service -> /usr/lib/systemd/user/omarchy-idle-inhibit.service
[exit status: 1]
```

With the omarchy-settings and omarchy-settings-dev hunk from omacom/omarchy-pkgs#210 applied to that same `master`, the file passes at 606bd454 and at 606bd454 merged into `quattro` e332dc97. `quattro` alone passes against unmodified `master`.

(`[exit status: N]` is the exit status of the whole pipeline, run with `pipefail`.)
</details>

<details><summary>Optional notes</summary>

- **Optional test improvement:** the first-run check reads the batch only up to the `omarchy-crash-watch.service` line. Appending the unit after that line puts it back into the batch, and the test still passes (`ok - first-run enables idle-inhibit separately …`). Checking the lines from the one ending in `enable --now \` up to the first line without a trailing backslash closes that gap (it fails for the unit before or after crash-watch).
- Open #10582 rewrites the same first-run batch into a loop that enables one unit at a time. If it lands, the separate enable here is no longer needed for isolation, though the fallback link still is until the packaging line lands.
- `migrations/1790440000.sh` still says in its comment that it owns `PowerManagement.Inhibit`. The unit `Description` and the command summary still say "names", and `inhibitorStatePath` in `Service.qml` is now unused.
</details>
